<description>
{
 "summary": "Fix oversized script decompression so that it overwrites the destination buffer with an OP_RETURN script rather than appending to it. It also adds a unit test verifying that decoding into a reused script with an unfinished push produces an unspendable script.",
 "problem": "When decoding an oversized compressed script into an existing script buffer that already contains an incomplete data push, appending OP_RETURN incorporates the byte into the pushed data instead of terminating the script, leaving the resulting script potentially spendable.",
 "evidence": [
  "Author description: \"The oversized-script fallback appends OP_RETURN to the destination instead of replacing it. If the destination already contains an unfinished push, the appended byte becomes pushed data and the result can remain spendable.\"",
  "Author notes the flaw appears latent in practice: \"This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.\""
 ],

<category name="tools" title="Tools and scripts">
## Covers

Command-line tools other than the node and its RPC client, and the
scripts under contrib: `bitcoin-tx`, `bitcoin-util`, the offline
`bitcoin-wallet` tool, the `bitcoin` wrapper, seed and asmap
generation, signet tooling, tracing scripts, and developer helper
scripts. Build and release scripts are build; test helpers are tests.
The Scripts and tools label is a strong prior.

## What matters here

Tools that operators and downstream projects depend on first: seed
generation, asmap, signet, and the wallet tool affect real deployments.
Then correctness of any tool that touches keys or transactions. Then
developer productivity tools that many contributors use. Then niche or
single-user scripts, which rank low regardless of size.
